root_cause.text: An off-by-one bug in the arm64 BPF JIT's check_imm() macro validated branch displacements against bits instead of bits-1, so signed immediates for B/B.cond/CBZ/CBNZ were accepted in an N+1-bit range rather than the true signed N-bit range.
root_cause.evidence: The patch changes check_imm() from shifting by (bits) to shifting by ((bits) - 1), and the commit/CVE explicitly states the old test admitted values in [-2^N, 2^N) instead of [-2^(N-1), 2^(N-1)), allowing values like check_imm19() displacements in [2^18, 2^19) to pass and then be masked by aarch64_insn_encode_immediate() into the imm19 field, flipping a forward branch into a backward one.

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix immediate range validation to correctly enforce signed fit within the requested bit width.
intent_record.what: The check_imm(bits, imm) macro was modified so both right-shift range checks use ((bits) - 1) instead of (bits): for positive immediates, (imm) >> ((bits) - 1), and for negative immediates, (~(imm)) >> ((bits) - 1).
intent_record.how: This tightens the immediate-width validation to treat the highest bit as the sign/value boundary, correctly rejecting values that do not fit in the specified signed bit width and avoiding acceptance of out-of-range immediates at runtime.

grouping_result.intent: Fix immediate range validation to correctly enforce signed fit within the requested bit width.

relevance_review.reason: The change directly fixes the immediate range validation logic to enforce proper signed N-bit bounds, which matches the root cause of accepting an N+1-bit range due to an off-by-one error in check_imm().

candidates.rationale: This range check uses shift-by-bits for positive signed immediates, which tests whether the value fits in bits+1 signed range rather than the intended signed bits range, causing the off-by-one acceptance.
This negative-immediate branch likewise uses shift-by-bits, allowing negative values that require bits+1 signed representation instead of enforcing the true signed bits-width limit.

vuln_statements.explanation: This range check is the core of the off-by-one bug: for positive signed immediates it shifts by bits instead of bits-1, so values needing N+1 signed bits are incorrectly accepted as fitting in N bits.
This is the corresponding negative-immediate side of the same conditional, also using bits instead of bits-1, which permits out-of-range negative signed immediates that require N+1 bits.

The vulnerable construct is present in `#define check_imm(bits, imm) do { if ((((imm) > 0) && ((imm) >> (bits))) || (((imm) < 0) && (~(imm) >> (bits)))) ... } while (0)`. This validates signed immediates using `>> (bits)` instead of the correct signed-N-bit bound based on `bits-1`, matching the stated root cause.
